rationales.explanation: Charles requires the initial car-seat purchase to lead into a broader relationship with the mother, and states that this belief is necessary for the business to work.
Charles cites his experience that parents are picky as a basis for skepticism about building a trusted, broad-use brand.
Charles asks what would be required to build a highly trusted brand comparable to a one-stop destination for modern parenting.
Charles is skeptical that the company can build the required trusted brand cost-effectively and expresses reservations about the cost of doing so.
Charles believes it will take a while before the brand reaches the level of trust needed for parents to use it for everything.

annotation_summary: Charles passes because he doubts the first product sale will expand into a larger customer relationship and questions whether the necessary trusted brand can be built cost-effectively within a reasonable timeframe.
